cell.n: Anatomy of a skeletal muscle cell

sarc.n: Myology: skeletal muscle (sarcomere, myosin and actin)

sr.n: Role of the sarcoplasmic reticulum in muscle cells

mg.n: Myasthenia gravis: causes, symptoms, treatment, pathology

trop.n: How tropomyosin and troponin regulate muscle contraction

From a whole muscle to one fiber: How is a skeletal muscle built?
Listen for the muscle, the fascicle, the muscle fiber and the myofibril, each one inside the one before.
Inside a muscle fiber: What are the T tubules and the SR?
Listen for the sarcolemma, the T tubules dipping into the fiber, and the sarcoplasmic reticulum wrapped around each myofibril.
The sarcomere: Listen for the Z discs, the thick filaments of myosin, the thin filaments of actin, and which bands each one makes.
Sliding filaments: Listen for the myosin heads pulling the thin filaments toward the middle while neither filament gets shorter.
The command arrives: What happens at the neuromuscular junction?
Listen for the action potential reaching the axon terminal, Ca2+ coming in, and ACh being released into the cleft.
ACh opens the receptor channels: What does ACh do at the motor end plate?
Listen for ACh binding to the receptors on the end plate and positive ions entering the muscle fiber.
One for one: How does the end plate start a muscle action potential?
Listen for ACh exciting the muscle cell at the end plate so that it fires and contracts.
Myasthenia gravis: What goes wrong in myasthenia gravis?
Listen for the antibodies against the ACh receptors and why the weakness gets worse with use.
From the T tubule to the SR: How does the action potential release Ca2+?
Listen for how the sarcoplasmic reticulum stores Ca2+ and releases it into the cytosol when the fiber is excited.
Can I see the whole chain from nerve to crossbridge?
Listen for the action potential traveling into the T tubules and the Ca2+ coming out of the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
Calcium uncovers the binding sites: How do troponin and tropomyosin control contraction?
Listen for tropomyosin covering the binding sites at rest and Ca2+ binding to troponin to move it.
When the SR cannot release Ca2+: Listen for why the myosin heads cannot do their work until Ca2+ binds to troponin C.
One turn of the crossbridge cycle: What does ATP do in the crossbridge cycle?
Listen for the order: ATP binds and the head lets go, ATP is split and the head cocks, phosphate leaves and the head pulls, then ADP leaves.
When the ATP runs out: Why does the head need ATP to let go?
Listen for the step where ATP binds and the myosin head releases actin, because that is the step that cannot happen without ATP.
Clearing the ACh: What happens to ACh after it is released?
Listen for acetylcholinesterase removing the ACh from the cleft.
Pumping the Ca2+ back: How does Ca2+ get back into the SR?
Listen for the sarcoplasmic reticulum taking Ca2+ back up so the cytosol level falls and the muscle relaxes.
When a shutoff fails: What happens if ACh is not removed?
Listen for the job acetylcholinesterase does, so you can work out what happens when it is blocked.
From command to contraction: Can I see the whole chain from nerve to crossbridge?
Listen for every step in order, from the action potential at the junction to crossbridge cycling.
